findings.claim: The opening fa makes the restricted facilitation clause read as a consequence or continuation, while innama narrows the rationale that follows.
findings.mechanism: The clause-initial connector meets innama and the later purpose lām: the verse enters as a linked consequence, then names the work for which facilitation serves.
findings.reader_payoff: The line opens as a continuation with a defined purpose, rather than as a detached statement.
findings.containment: The preceding promise or warning content is not present in this micro packet, so no specific antecedent is reconstructed.

findings.title: Restriction with an independent clause

findings.mechanism: The attached mā keeps inna from taking the next verb as an ordinary governed nominal complement; the later purpose clauses fill the restricted rationale.
findings.reader_payoff: The restriction is carried across a full action and its stated purposes, not merely attached to a noun.

findings.mechanism: Innamā precedes the facilitation verb, and the purpose lām governs glad tidings before wa carries the same purpose over to warning; that contact gives the restricted clause a communicative end.
findings.reader_payoff: Ease becomes directed work in the verse, with glad tidings and warning both filling the purpose.
findings.containment: The local syntax does not say that no other property of the revelation exists; the restriction is bounded to this facilitation claim and its stated rationale.

epistemic.reason: The particle, purpose marker, coordination, and attachment evidence are all in the focus record.

findings.reader_payoff: The wording shows an act that prepares the revelation for use, not merely a revelation that happens to be easy.
findings.containment: The local form grounds caused facilitation; wider repetitions of the formula are not used here.

epistemic.reason: The QAC morphology and the focus word-analysis description agree on perfect Form II and its object suffix.

findings.title: Ease made ready for use

findings.mechanism: The verb carries ease and preparation; bi-lisānika names a concrete means, and the purpose verbs show what becomes usable through it. Their contact shifts ease from an abstract quality toward an accessible message.
findings.reader_payoff: The facilitation can be felt as readiness for actual speaking and reception.
findings.containment: This is root pressure under the local Form II making-easy sense, not a claim about modern encoding or a separate technical process.

epistemic.reason: The core ease sense is grounded; the preparedness extension is retained as a local relation with the named medium and purposes.

findings.title: The first half of a repeated instrument
findings.claim: The first bi-hi begins a local frame that returns after the warning verb.
findings.mechanism: The pronoun follows tubashshira and appears again after tundhira; the first occurrence lets the later act be heard as using the same compact referent.

findings.containment: This finding treats the first occurrence as setup; the second occurrence retains its own role in completing the parallel.

findings.title: The second occurrence completes the parallel
findings.claim: The repeated bi-hi completes a balanced frame in which the same facilitated revelation is used for two different speech acts.
findings.mechanism: After the coordinated purpose verbs, the second pronoun returns in the same form as the first and closes the pair; the repeated referent holds steady while the function changes.
findings.reader_payoff: A single revelation can remain constant across glad tidings and warning.
findings.containment: The structural parallel does not erase the different verbs or audiences and does not identify a separate source for either act.

epistemic.reason: The exact parallel and its placement after the second purpose verb are supplied.

findings.title: Warning through the same revelation

findings.mechanism: The pronoun repeats after tundhira and is resolved to the same revelation; the warning is therefore mediated through that message, not through a separately named threat source.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning half stays attached to the revelation that was made easy for the first purpose.
findings.containment: The shared instrument does not make warning and good news the same act or audience.

epistemic.reason: The local repetition and referent resolution are directly supported.

findings.title: The revelation as message and means

findings.containment: The phrase permits content and instrument shading; it does not make the recipient the pronoun's referent.

epistemic.reason: The supplied attachment and referent analysis establish the relation, while content-versus-instrument remains a bounded grammatical range.

findings.containment: The local definiteness does not supply the omitted beneficiary parallels or make the group the warning's object.

findings.title: An active self-guarding identity

findings.reader_payoff: The first audience is seen as people actively putting protection between themselves and harm.
findings.containment: The local form describes the named recipient class; it does not claim a specific response to this announcement or import cross-ayah parallels.

findings.title: Repeated consonant pressure

findings.title: One prepared interface, two audience effects
findings.claim: The focus presents a prepared speech interface through which one facilitated revelation branches into glad tidings for a self-guarding audience and warning for a resistant collective.
findings.mechanism: Yassarnāhu carries ease and readiness; lisānika names the language and speech interface; the repeated bi-hi keeps one message attached to tubashshira and tundhira. Al-muttaqīn and qawman luddā then supply distinct recipient postures. The supplied HFT before/after contrast is preserved: before, the verse merely says the revelation is linguistically easy and carries reward and threat; after, the same speakable vehicle produces joy or alarm according to protective or adversarial posture.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees one facilitated utterance prepared for human speech and turned toward two audiences, rather than two separate messages or sources.
findings.containment: The local syntax supports two functions and audiences; the branch roles and before/after relation come from a legacy_unbound reconstruction, so no audience response is asserted as achieved and neither purpose replaces the plain facilitation claim.

findings.title: Advance notice that can awaken protection
findings.claim: The coordinated good-news and warning acts can be heard as two forms of advance notice: one discloses beginnings, while the other reports danger early enough to invite caution.
findings.mechanism: The first-signs facet of glad tidings meets the coordinated warning verb; warning names a resistant target, while the self-guarding audience supplies a protective orientation. Yassarnāhu makes the notice ready before outcomes arrive. The supplied HFT before/after contrast is preserved: before, good news comforts one fixed group while warning condemns another; after, both acts are prospective signals that confirm protection in one audience while still inviting it in the other.
findings.reader_payoff: The two acts remain different but become forward-looking communications, and protection appears as a possible response rather than only a fixed label.
findings.containment: No benefit, danger, response time, or actual change by either audience is specified. The protective endpoint and reconstructed before/after relation remain qualified HFT attributions; the two named audiences are not collapsed.

epistemic.reason: The focus coordinates and local syntax are supplied, but the advance-notice synthesis is a legacy_unbound reconstruction and is kept as an attributed, bounded interpretation.
